title: Stakeholder signal mesh and decision fabric for customer-driven roadmap
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Executive and enterprise stakeholder asks arrive through multiple channels (CS tickets, renewal conversations, executive escalations, support incidents) and currently get manually translated into roadmap candidates. We lack a single, auditable scoring and commitment fabric that ties signal intensity to a predictable commitment runway.

Goal: Build a 'decision fabric' that synthesizes signals into ranked roadmap candidates, surfaces recommended commitment windows, and exposes a simulator to model acceptance risk vs. runway impact. Outputs should be actionable for PMs and explainable for sales/CS.

Scope: 1) Define canonical signal taxonomy (renewal risk, ARR weight, escalations, number of impacted endpoints, production latency/cost regressions, security/compliance requests, strategic partner gravity). 2) Create a normalized scoring model with adjustable weights and explainability breadcrumbs. 3) Integrate signal ingestion: CS Zendesk / Gainsight hooks, Sales notes (Drive templates), SSO incident logs, support triage tags. 4) Lightweight simulator UI in Console (read-only for initial phase) to model how accepting an item shifts commitment runway and risks. 5) Document escalation-to-commitment playbook and guardrails (SLA, credits, canary requirements).

Success metrics: - Time from customer ask to triage decision reduced from median 18 days -> <= 5 days. - Percentage of high-contact accounts with explicit commitment window recorded in system: 0% -> 85% for qualified asks. - Simulated roadmap adherence: less than 15% of accepted asks require scope rollback in 90 days.

Acceptance criteria: - Signal taxonomy doc published and reviewed by CS/Revenue/Engineering. - Scoring model prototype implemented and validated on a 6-month backlog sample with qualitative review from three account leads. - Simulator MVP in Console allowing PMs to toggle up to 10 pending asks and visualize runway + risk delta. - Playbook published with decision thresholds and escalation steps.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full two-way automation with pulsed executive nudges and automated contract amendments.

Notes on trade-offs: We prioritize explainability over completely automated prioritization for first two cycles. The scoring model will be intentionally conservative on ARR weighting to avoid over-committing to small-dollar but noisy signals.
